status: Meets the Bench Standard bar on Opus (53/53, no invented facts, URLs or alt text). On Haiku it beats every comparison and reached 48/53, but still guesses occasionally (a suggested alt text, a softened replacement claim); recommended for larger models.
method: 8 evals (3 traps), expectations written before any run. Round 1 ran the skill, no skill, and the closest public skill (Corey Haines' copy-editing 1.3.0) on Haiku, and the skill and no skill on Opus, in fresh headless agents graded blind by a separate grader. Rounds 2-4 re-ran the skill as it was revised.
losses_and_open_issues: Haiku misses unsupported claims without a number ('Group owners tell us the consolidated view is what they were missing') in every round
Haiku under time pressure suggests softened replacement claims ('a leading', 'trusted by owners across Canada') instead of deleting
Haiku occasionally guesses alt text or adds a fact to a suggested meta description, and over-escalates hedged rules of thumb ('about 65% of sales') to blockers
Round 1, without any skill: copy-editing invented a testimonial name, a pricing URL, statistics and a HIPAA claim; no-skill Opus over-flagged a clean newsletter as not ready (660 words)
Every run, all configs, left the original files unchanged
